page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance from the E2 family. It features 4 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at 2.2 GHz, configured with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is positioned for workloads that prioritize memory capacity over raw compute speed. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU benchmarks place the instance in the bottom 25 percent, reflecting its cost-efficient architecture. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores fall into the bottom 10 percent. However, the PassMark memory score achieves an average rating in the middle 50 percent, demonstrating stable memory performance relative to its compute capabilities.

The qualitative cost profile of the e2-highmem-4 is highly favorable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-frequency CPU performance or local NVMe storage. It offers a cost-effective alternative to premium memory-optimized instances by utilizing a balanced, resource-dense configuration. This makes it suitable for small-to-medium databases, caching layers, and memory-bound background processing tasks where compute demands are moderate.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-4 is a cost-effective, memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 4 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.2 GHz, this instance features 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark data shows that while CPU performance and web serving throughput reside in the lower percentiles, the instance maintains average memory performance. This resource profile makes the e2-highmem-4 highly suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not demand intensive CPU processing, such as caching servers, small database deployments, and moderate data processing tasks.
